newsitem.title: CANADA: Poll gives Canadian Liberals 24-point lead.
newsitem.headline: Poll gives Canadian Liberals 24-point lead.

text.p: Prime Minister Jean Chretien's Liberals command a 24-point lead over their nearest campaign rivals, but voters could easily switch allegiances, a new poll released on Monday showed.

The poll, conducted for the Canadian Broadcasting Corp (CBC), put the Liberals at 44 percent among decided voters, followed by the Conservatives at 20 percent, Reform at 15 percent, the New Democrats at 11 percent and the Bloc Quebecois at eight percent.
The CBC said half the Liberal and Conservative supporters said they might change their minds, while Reform's support was firmer.
An Angus Reid Poll published by Southam News on Saturday also showed a 24-point margin among decided voters -- Liberals 42 percent, Conservatives 18 percent and Reform 16 percent.
But a Gallup Canada released on Friday showed the Liberals at 55 percent and the Conservatives at only 15 percent.
The CBC poll, conducted among 2,541 citizens from April 17-22 in Quebec by CROP and in the rest of Canada by Environics, also gave Chretien the highest popularity rating.

Thirty-six percent thought he would make the best prime minister, followed by 21 percent for the Conservatives' Jean Charest, 13 percent for Reform's Preston Manning and seven percent for the NDP's Alexa McDonough.

Since the separatist Bloc Quebecois and Reform had strong regional strength, they seized a larger number of seats in Parliament than their vote numbers indicated in the 1993 election and might do so again in the June 2 election.
Thirty-seven percent of those polled rated unemployment as the most pressing issue and 14 percent each rated national unity and the fiscal deficit as the most important.
A breakdown for Quebec, showing the Liberals marginally ahead of the Bloc Quebecois, was released on Monday morning.
The CBC said the national poll carried a margin of error of two percentage points 19 times out of 20.
